subject: Marketplace entitlement pathways and SKU eligibility for multi-cloud GTM
messages:

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing questions + co-sell ask

Connor —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We moved this internally and the procurement team wants clarity on two things before we can sign up for a pilot via marketplace:

1) Which Redwood SKUs will be eligible for AWS co-sell vs. Azure vs. GCP? We have workloads that must stay in us-west and eu-west primarily.
2) What does the entitlement path look like for a customer that signs in via a cloud marketplace listing but needs Dedicated capacity (reserved) in our AWS account?

Attached is a simple matrix with our expected initial usage. Can you put together a short replacement-flow we can show procurement (they asked for a diagram and the expected billing flow)?

If we can get that this week, I can keep momentum with the procurement and legal teams.

—Priya
Director of Cloud Ops, AtlasAnalytics

From: connor.obrien@redwood.com <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing questions + co-sell ask

Hi Priya —

Great questions. Quick summary up front: we can support marketplace purchase flows that land customers either on Hosted (Redwood API) or trigger a Dedicated capacity provisioning on a customer AWS subscription via a private offer/entitlement mapping. GCP and Azure have slightly different entitlement mechanics; below I sketched the recommended SKUs and the preferred GTM routes.

High-level recommendations (short):
- AWS: list two SKUs ("redwood-hosted-standard", "redwood-dedicated-reserved"). Offer co-sell for both but use private-offer entitlements for Dedicated so the purchase can automatically map to the reserved pool and the customer's account linkage is established.
- Azure: list a single "redwood-hosted" SKU initially; use marketplace listing + Azure Marketplace Managed Application to enable Dedicated on demand. Co-sell requires field engagement for Dedicated.
- GCP: prefer a single universal listing and use Cloud Marketplace Procurement + onboarding script to attach a Dedicated instance group if needed. Co-sell for hosted is straightforward; Dedicated requires an ops handover.

What I'll attach: 1) a one-page entitlement diagram for procurement, 2) an updated SKU eligibility matrix (I updated your sheet), 3) a short co-sell checklist we use for marketplace ops.

Action items for us:
- Marissa: confirm co-sell enablement checklist and typical discount bands used for private offers (will feed procurement expectation).
- Karthik: validate Azure managed app approach with partner engineering and confirm if we can auto-provision Dedicated via ARM templates.
- Ben: confirm GCP procurement flow (billing export mapping) and whether we need a separate listing per region.

Priya — I'll get the diagram and updated matrix to you by EOD Tues. If procurement wants, we can put them on a 30-minute call with our marketplace ops lead.

Thanks,
Connor
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachments: entitlement_flow.drawio, co_sell_checklist.pdf

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, pri...@atlasanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing questions + co-sell ask

Connor — quick notes after sync with Partner Eng:

- Azure: Managed Application route is OK but has two constraints: (1) we need a customer-maintained resource group (we can't fully own the Dedicated VM in their VNET without a managed resource approach) and (2) we should avoid listing a Dedicated SKU until we have a hardened ARM template and playbook. For procurement messaging, we should present Azure Dedicated as "Available via managed app; field-assisted setup".
- AWS: Private Offers can auto-entitle usage to our reserved pools via an entitlement token exchange. We'll need a small onboarding lambda in the customer's account to stitch their AWS ARN to our Dedicated pool. That lambda is lightweight and ops-approved.
- GCP: There's no clean entitlement token equivalent. Best path is a linked service account and a short runbook where our onboarding runner creates a VPC peering + routes traffic to the Dedicated pool. It requires a little more manual setup.

I'll update the entitlement diagram to reflect these constraints and add the minimal automation steps for AWS and GCP.

Karthik
Sr. Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: AWS Marketplace Team <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: pri...@atlasanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing questions + co-sell ask

Hi Connor / Marissa —

Thanks for the outline. For AWS private offers the entitlement token approach you describe is supported; we recommend the following be included in the private offer metadata: productCode, entitlementMapping (ARN), and a single-use onboarding URL that triggers the entitlement lambda. Please note the private offer review takes ~5 business days after submission.

Next steps we recommend for AtlasAnalytics:
- Submit private offer draft with your expected pricing tiers.
- Add the entitlement lambda repository link to the offer notes so our compliance team can review the bootstrap.
- Schedule a co-sell planning call with the AWS field rep (I can intro if you share the preferred window).

If helpful, we can also share a sample private offer payload.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Ops
